answer: Verifying 1,000 repair tasks requires an atlas of assigned faults to ensure each agent performs unique work. Each agent must mirror its input to generate a checksum, and a network echo confirms the work matches the assigned task. The honest cost is 1,000 units of compute, while 1,000 fakes incur 1,000,000 units because they cannot reuse an atlas state. If an echo of a prior result appears, the mirror verification triggers a permanent stake-slash.
